title: How are you creating 3d models?
author: Desperate-Day-3491
selftext:
as far as my research has brought me the options are platforms like meshy or tripo, using an llm connected to blender, or local models like hunyuan. So far I found online platforms to be expensive since I'm mostly just testing ideas, maybe if I had a full scale project in mind. llms using blender are just not good enough yet, ill burn through all my usage trying to make one crappy model. And running locally is just not an option for me.

Just wondering what yall have been having success with.

replies.author: sunnystormy64
replies.body:
You have to:

1. Install ComfyUI

2. Decide whether you want to use TripoSplat or Trellis 2 / Pixal3D for 3D mesh gen (I can't recall if their deployment of Hunyuan 3D 2.1 has textures, but use the first two I mentioned)

3. Have images of things you want to create ready for 3D asset gen

If you feel you need more assistance, ping me, or swing by PixelArtistry's channel on YouTube.

comments.author: ThreeDMK
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/mabcrxb6d3uh1.jpeg?width=1320&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=bf69d87a5dd2289e859b543472fadca4fd51cde5

Was just checking on progress while at work.  I am using headless blender + mcp + opus5.5 to build assets for me while I’m in the office.  I have it orchestrating the work, connected via remote control, I just follow along while doing other things.  It’s actually pretty wild.  

I spend a lot of time documenting what I want and then have Claude build scripts to automate the creation of things, then compare it to what I am looking for.  If I really need to I work with Claude to do things directly, and if I really need something bespoke I just jump into Blender myself now and make things work.

By establishing baselines and standards my create themes seem to be sticking together really well.

replies.author: necronomicoder
replies.body: What orchestrator are you using?  Just Claude app?  I am having Claude manage codex but it's a bit janky

replies.author: ThreeDMK
replies.body:
At the front it is just Claude’s desktop app.  

It has a custom MCP I built that connect to all of my information.  Registry for all my code and systems, a graph db for context, a task manager that is a clone of Jira I built that is modified for agent usage, and mountains of standards and governance.

Whenever I ask it to do things it follows a deterministic process that is well defined.  This way I can fire off large bodies of work and then let it build while I do other things.  :)

Automate all the things.  :)

replies.author: necronomicoder
replies.body:
Neat.  I just use forgejo for tasks, code, ci together.  MCP for that isn't really needed and used more tokens that just a simple skill in the end. 

I'm curious what the graph context gets you?  I capture things as skills or docs and just clear context between runs, which are days to weeks.

What I don't have is central, cross server orchestration.  I can see that might be where the graph context comes in, but Claude code UI doesn't really do packing of agents or orchestrating multiple loops (one chat per task bound to a server).

replies.author: ThreeDMK
replies.body:
I should have been clear earlier.  I had 4 remote control conversations going today while at work.  3 on one project, one on another.

3 of these are still running this evening:  
\- DAW updates to support history and change rollback.  I built my own sound toy  
\- Track updates to my game now that this theme is built and ready for use  
\- Production setup and deploy in AWS.  One of my other games failed a playtest earlier today.  My home internet provider did not like 20 people trying to hit my personal webserver.  :(  Moving the entire deployment to AWS now.

All of this is run through Claude Desktop conversations that work as orchestration against my development harness. Everything contextual is managed there.  Instructions.  Governance.  Things that help steer it in the right direction to complete my tasks for me.  I do not use AI to think for me as much as just glue between a lot of automation.  It allows me to use cheaper and smaller models for efficiently.

https://preview.redd.it/6er8bbg6y5uh1.png?width=1152&format=png&auto=webp&s=42fb2edb50c94b96a3e3fdd890b311383d348ec4

This is the visualization of that data.  Blue is governance, everything else is a project with its own content.  I have anywhere from 3-8 different orchestrations running at any point in time across multiple computers.  All of them feed from the same group of APIs on a docker server running on my network.  :)

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: How long on average does it take for generation? I've been interested in the Opus+Blender pipeline, and the art style I'm going for is pretty stylized/semi-low poly, so the models *should* (in my head at least) be easier to handle than something HD.

replies.author: ThreeDMK
replies.body:
I originally went the high-res route and was happy for the first few passes, but it really started to struggle on some of my larger tracks.

https://preview.redd.it/6u9hzh0nu5uh1.png?width=3214&format=png&auto=webp&s=fbffa9730d42030985d45a5edd56309cb3dcc547

Pikes Peak.  The map generation takes about 4-5 minutes overall.

With the new art style:  
"A full kit build produces 1,673 pieces in 13,313 files and takes 82 seconds" - Current theme  
"A Low build averages about 24 seconds per track. I timed three tracks just now with [`build.py`](http://build.py) `--low`:" - Current full track build process.  Medium is running now and will likely take much longer.  Generating all of the prebuilt items first has helped a ton though.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Thanks for the response, and wow that’s a lot quicker than I was expecting. Looks very promising.

replies.author: ThreeDMK
replies.body: I have been super impressed with it so far.  I really wanted to go the high quality route, but I am not nearly as skilled in 3d work as I am software development.  If 3d is your thing, you could likely make things far more efficiently and quickly than I am.  :)

comments.author: ThreeDMK
comments.body:
The blue dots are all nodes that contain operational governance.  Code standards, scaffolding, library details, jobs/tasks/skills, etc.  all mapped together.  The outer groups are projects. Some of them reference inner nodes.

This also handles project details and high level state for the things I am working on.  All work that I do touches this in some manner to keep things organized.  

This graph is accessible by all of my computers, and in some cases my sub agents interact with it on their own for info.  Because they are nodes I can reference smaller items directly, saving context.  Local models love this stuff.  :)

I also should have been clear, this 3d work is one of four conversations I was monitoring today while working.  I also have a DAW building me music for my game, along with new tracks being built and improved.  Up to 68 now after today.  :)
